Display-only inspector honesty, closing the 2026-08-24 demo's trust amplifier (postmortem section 2): the side panel showed per-item conf 0.95 with no link back to a document-level success_with_warning. Panel half reads the response's own doc_status plus the item's evidence.warnings — which IS validate.py score()'s hits list, so the panel names exactly the codes that cost the item WARN_PENALTY and inherits ADR-018's expected_item_missing exclusion instead of defining 'item-targeted' a second time in the display layer. Banner half surfaces unattributed_content's existing figure with validate.py's own understatement caveat (up to 9.7 points, interior gaps uncounted); no new number is computed in the view layer, because the envelope coverage field is D8's and a second producer for a derived figure is the defect S9/display_text already taught this repo. THE WHOLE PR IS ONE LESSON ABOUT WHAT A STATIC TEXT PIN CAN CLAIM. Round 1 (4 M / 3 L): the new check pinned that the qualifier's text was PRESENT, never that it was reached or called — severing coverageStrip's call, or an early return in docQual/itemQual, restored the demo defect with the full gate green. Round 2 (2 M standing + 1 L): the implementer strengthened the mechanism (whole-body _js_block equality) and the reviewer falsified the still-unchanged guarantee again — _js_block reads the FIRST 'function <fn>(' while JS runs the LAST, so a duplicate declaration neutered any helper at invariant 61/61 and fast 124/124; separately conf ${esc(it.confidence)} named the field, printed a bare number, and was invisible to the widened scan. Both reproduced independently by the orchestrator before relay. Round 3: APPROVED. The convergent move was NOT a fourth stronger pin. The orchestrator's round-2 guidance was that strengthening alone had twice invited a fresh falsification, and the implementer took it: the 'WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT GUARANTEE' paragraph was replaced in all four places by a description of the TEXT the pins assert, an explicit statement that no static read of one file can assert what the page RENDERS, the concrete holes, and the load-bearing sentence that the hole list is ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT EXHAUSTIVE. Read green as 'the pinned text is present and unique', never as 'the defect is impossible'. Round 3's five LOWs (R10 spaced-duplicate declaration, R11 nested-${ scan miss, R12 one of four copies out of sync, R13 stale probe counts, R14 dead branch) are all further spellings of that same ceiling, all non-blocking by the reviewer's own flag, and all went to debt rather than a fourth escalation — logged with the reasoning that chasing spellings one reviewer-round at a time is the pattern rounds 1-3 showed does not converge. The whole loop was about the difference between pinning a VALUE and pinning the NAME OF A VARIABLE. D12 ships a contract, not a mapping: ADR-026 s.a's refusal of a raw-to-normalized offset map was restated in the implementer prompt as a hard boundary rather than left to be rediscovered, and nothing in the diff approximates one. app.py was byte-unchanged after the first commit — every repair round landed in the CHECK, because the code was right and the pin was weak. R1 (MEDIUM, the only one): WIRE_NORMALIZED pinned the two expressions that MENTION `norm` and never where `norm` came from, so `norm = hit[1]` made /api/normalized/{token} serve the RAW FILING under a matching X-Normalized-SHA256 header with the whole gate green — the published recipe's step 3 broken for every consumer, and the case's own triage note claiming the payload was pinned. Repair 1 added the bindings plus a regex NORM_BINDERS guard; round 2 (R4) defeated it with `norm = hit[2]; norm = hit[1]` on one physical line — a line-anchored regex counts that as one binding. Repair 2 replaced the regex with an ast walk counting Name(ctx=Store) in the named function: the property itself rather than a better pattern. Round 3 (R6) then showed even Store-counting is not 'every binding form' — a match-capture rebinds with zero Store nodes — and named the real ceiling: `hit = (hit[0], hit[1], hit[1])` before the pinned binding serves the raw filing with every norm guard satisfied, and NO binding-count guard can ever close it. That is the inherent ceiling of allow-list text pinning in repo_hygiene, so the fix was to STATE the ceiling, not build against it. THREE ROUNDS, ONE DEFECT CLASS, ESCALATING SCOPE: every round after the first was a committed artifact claiming more than the code established (R1 triage note, R4 'binds norm exactly once' in four places, R5 'executed, not just a spelling check' where the executed comparison was logically implied by the line above it and had zero falsification power, R6 'every binding form Python has'). R5's fix DELETED the dead comparison rather than leaving it under corrected prose — keeping the check would have kept the thing that made the sentence tempting. TWO SELF-CAUGHT IMPLEMENTER DEFECTS, both reported unprompted: NORM_BINDERS first keyed on the route decorator so the end-of-function scan hit the handler's own `def` and scanned an empty slice (red for the wrong reason, and green the instant anyone wrote the expected count as 0), caught by READING the red output rather than counting it; and a third copy of R9's false 'shipped' claim in a sibling artifact the finding had not named, corrected and flagged as a deliberate one-sentence overrun of a bounded pass. ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS rather than trusting the resolution artifacts: reproduced R4's same-line mutant before spending a round on it (0 failures confirmed), and re-ran both R4 mutants against the ast guard after (both red). ROUTING: two LOW findings (R2, and R4/R5) were routed to REPAIR against the LOW-to-debt rule on one stated test applied consistently — a committed artifact asserting as verified something the diff does not establish is the blocking condition regardless of severity, and R2's broken line was inside the very README recipe the task exists to publish. R3 (line-ref drift in an unrelated debt row this diff merely shifted) went to debt on the same test. NO FOURTH REVIEW ROUND WAS RUN, deliberately and on the record: round 3 returned APPROVED with four LOW residuals for which the reviewer had dictated literal replacement wording, so they were applied as a bounded correction pass — orchestrator verified the diff contained nothing beyond them — rather than spending a round re-reviewing a reviewer's own words. The last reviewer verdict on record is round 3 APPROVED. Gate never went red in any round; digests byte-identical to pre-D12 across all 61 filings (dev 8c002dce, heldout 51de5a11) at every commit.
